newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy needs '97 minibudget if exceeds goals - Monti.
newsitem.headline: Italy needs '97 minibudget if exceeds goals - Monti.

text.p: Italy will need further budget deficit cutting measures next year in addition to those it is already planning in its 1997 budget bill if it does not meet its economic targets, European Commissioner Mario Monti said.
Monti told reporters at a meeting in Rome he was optimistic about the possibility that Italy would take part in European economic and monetary union (EMU) at its outset.
"I'm fairly optimistic because the objectives Italy needs to pursue have been set," he said.
But he said an additional budget in 1997 "will be inevitable if the deficit objectives which the government has set give way to overshoots....I cannot say at the moment if there will be overshoots."
Criteria for taking part in EMU at its projected 1999 start stipulate among other things that member countries must have a deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio of three percent in 1997.
Italy, whose bulging budget deficit is projected to be around 6.6 percent of GDP this year, wants to be part of the single currency at its start.

The centre-left government has set a target ratio of 3.1 percent deficit to GDP for 1997 and is currently pushing a budget package aimed a deficit-cutting measures worth 62.5 trillion lire through parliament.
